title: NEET-UG Exam Strategy
summary: Mastering the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test for Medical aspirants.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction

The NEET-UG Exam offers candidates an incredible opportunity for a secure and prestigious career. It requires candidates to clear a multi-tier selection process that rigorously tests their aptitude, physical fitness, and overall capability. Thousands of aspirants apply every year, making it one of the most competitive career paths available today. Strategic preparation based on the latest examination syllabus is vital to stand out and succeed.

## Eligibility Criteria

| Parameter | Requirements |
|---|---|
| **Educational Qualification** | Must have passed 12th standard with Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Biotechnology, and English as core subjects. |
| **Nationality** | Indian Nationals, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), Overseas Citizen of India (OCI), Persons with Indian Origin (PIO), and Foreign Nationals. |
| **Stream/Subject** | PCB (Physics, Chemistry, Biology). |
| **Minimum Percentage** | 50% for General, 45% for General-PwD, and 40% for SC/ST/OBC in PCB. |
| **Document Verification** | Valid ID proof, educational certificates, domicile, and category certificates must be produced in original at the final stages. |
| **Additional Diplomas** | N/A |
| **Computer Literacy** | N/A |

## Written Exam Pattern

| Subject / Section | Total Questions | Maximum Marks | Duration / Time Allowed | Negative Marking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Physics** | 50 Questions (Attempt 45) | 180 Marks | Combined with other sections | -1 per incorrect answer |
| **Chemistry** | 50 Questions (Attempt 45) | 180 Marks | Combined with other sections | -1 per incorrect answer |
| **Botany** | 50 Questions (Attempt 45) | 180 Marks | Combined with other sections | -1 per incorrect answer |
| **Zoology** | 50 Questions (Attempt 45) | 180 Marks | Combined with other sections | -1 per incorrect answer |
| **Overall Grand Total** | **200 Questions (Attempt 180)**| **720 Marks**| **200 Minutes** | **Applicable uniformly** |

## Preparation Strategy Overview

| Preparation Phase | Recommended Action Plan for Candidates |
|---|---|
| **Phase 1: Foundation Building** | Understand the complete syllabus thoroughly. Collect standard reference books, study materials, and begin clearing fundamental concepts across all subjects. |
| **Phase 2: Intensive Practice** | Solve previous year question papers. Enroll in structured mock test series. Analyze performance metrics, identify weak areas, and allocate extra time to improve them. |
| **Phase 3: Final Revision** | Create short, crisp notes for quick recall. Focus on current affairs of the last six months. Avoid picking up completely new topics just before the exam. |
| **Phase 4: Physical & Mental Health**| Maintain a balanced diet, ensure adequate sleep, and incorporate daily physical exercises to clear medical and physical efficiency tests effortlessly. |

We emphasize to all candidates that the details provided above are intended to give you a clear, structured overview of the recruitment framework. Please note that specific numbers, dates, and requirements are subject to modifications as determined by the official recruiting authority. It is highly advised to continually reference the official notification for the most accurate, binding, and up-to-date parameters. Candidates should align their preparation strategies rigorously with the official guidelines to ensure maximum compliance and readiness for all stages.
